chapter: Split, hospital and decline of tap
title: The high chair, his parents and the word remember
summary: Green recalls his mother seating him in a baby chair, his father and Uncle Saul lecturing him, and learning manners and memory in Fitzgerald.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And she said, "Come here and get up in the chair," and she set me up in a high -- what do you call it -- baby chair, you know. "Yes, ma'am," you see. I got up there, you know, and she said, "My, my," and she went back towards the stove, you know, whenever I see my mother going towards the stove I would get happy, you see, because I knew I was going to get a piece offie or some goodies fromsomewhere, you know. So, I kept on, and eventually my Daddy would come home, you know. Well, I was happy again, see, because I had something to say about that day to my parents, you see, and I was always getting lectured and my Uncle named Saul -- he would lecture me before

I would arrive at school, on the way to kindergarten, you know. And, so, I had something nice to say to my parents, my Daddy. Of course, I would never -- I was an only child and I would never know when I was going to get asked a question, you know. But if one would ask a question, you know, if the other one didn't answer the question that that one would ask, then I would have to answer it, you see. But sometimes I would get two questions to answer, so I figured, well, now I've got them. I've got them now. I'm going to tell you something, you see. But a baby's not supposed to do that, you know. You have to have good manners, so that's what I was learning -- the language of manners -- good manners like that. And I think that's what really encouraged me to try to tap dance, you know, in the future, see. Because I wanted to keep company with memory -- remember, remember, remember. See, I was always hearing that word -- remember, you know, from different people, you know. So, I started climbing trees and watching the people, you know. Well, I could hear something they're going to say, you know, and that's mostly the word I used to hear -- remember, remember. I remember, you know.
And also because your mother and father liked when you talked about dancing and things like that.
Yes, they did, they liked that, you know. Like, if you say something about someone that was getting baptized in the Swanee River, you see -- the Swanee River used

to come through Fitzgerald, Georgia -- some parts, you know. It goes on the wy through the Everglades, some way, because it's semi-tropical, you see, Fitzgerald, Georgia, see. You could see the heat waves at certain hours of the day. You could look out your window or climb up, you know, or something. You could even chase -- I thought you could chase a heat wave, you know. I said, "Isn't that strange?" And people used to try to read your fortune, you know. They liked that -- the grown-ups, you know, and elders, you see.
